paragraphs.en: Up until a few decades ago, our visions of the future were largely – though by no means uniformly – glowingly positive. Science and technology would cure all the ills of humanity, leading to lives of fulfilment and opportunity for all.
paragraphs.zh: 直到几十年前，我们对未来的想象大体上还是充满光明、积极乐观的，尽管绝非人人如此。科学技术将医治人类的一切弊病，使每个人都过上充实而充满机遇的生活。

paragraphs.en: Now utopia has grown unfashionable, as we have gained a deeper appreciation of the range of threats facing us, from asteroid strike to epidemic flu and to climate change. You might even be tempted to assume that humanity has little future to look forward to.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，随着我们更深刻地认识到所面临的各种威胁——从小行星撞击、流感大流行到气候变化——乌托邦式的设想已经不再流行。你甚至可能忍不住认为，人类几乎没有什么值得期待的未来。

paragraphs.en: But such gloominess is misplaced. The fossil record shows that many species have endured for millions of years – so why shouldn’t we? Take a broader look at our species’ place in the universe, and it becomes clear that we have an excellent chance of surviving for tens, if not hundreds, of thousands of years. Look up Homo sapiens in the “Red List” of threatened species of the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and you will read: “Listed as Least Concern as the species is very widely distributed, adaptable, currently increasing, and there are no major threats resulting in an overall population decline.”
paragraphs.zh: 但这种悲观并无道理。化石记录表明，许多物种已经延续了数百万年，人类为什么不能呢？从更广阔的视角看待人类在宇宙中的位置，就会清楚地发现：即使不能生存数十万年，我们也极有可能生存数万年。在国际自然保护联盟（IUCN）的濒危物种“红色名录”中查找智人，你会读到：“列为无危物种，因为该物种分布非常广泛，适应能力强，目前数量仍在增加，而且不存在导致种群总量下降的重大威胁。”

paragraphs.en: So what does our deep future hold? A growing number of researchers and organisations are now thinking seriously about that question. For example, the Long Now Foundation has as its flagship project a mechanical clock that is designed to still be marking time thousands of years hence.
paragraphs.zh: 那么，遥远的未来究竟等待着我们什么呢？越来越多的研究人员和组织，如今正在认真思考这个问题。例如，“恒今基金会”的旗舰项目是一座机械钟，其设计目标是在数千年之后仍然能够计时。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps willfully, it may be easier to think about such lengthy timescales than about the more immediate future. The potential evolution of today’s technology, and its social consequences, is dazzlingly complicated, and it’s perhaps best left to science fiction writers and futurologists to explore the many possibilities we can envisage. That’s one reason why we have launched Arc, a new publication dedicated to the near future.
paragraphs.zh: 也许是出于有意选择，比起较为近期的未来，思考如此漫长的时间尺度反而更容易。当今技术可能如何演变，以及它会带来什么社会后果，复杂得令人眼花缭乱；我们能够设想的诸多可能性，或许最好留给科幻作家和未来学家去探索。这也是我们创办专门关注近期未来的新刊物《Arc》的原因之一。

paragraphs.en: But take a longer view and there is a surprising amount that we can say with considerable assurance. As so often, the past holds the key to the future: we have now identified enough of the long-term patterns shaping the history of the planet, and our species, to make evidence-based forecasts about the situations in which our descendants will find themselves.
paragraphs.zh: 但把眼光放得更长远一些，我们就会发现，有相当多的事情可以作出颇有把握的判断，其数量之多令人惊讶。一如往常，过去蕴藏着通向未来的钥匙：对于塑造地球和人类历史的长期规律，我们如今已认识得足够多，可以有根据地预测后代将面临的处境。

paragraphs.en: This long perspective makes the pessimistic view of our prospects seem more likely to be a passing fad. To be sure, the future is not all rosy. But we are now knowledgeable enough to reduce many of the risks that threatened the existence of earlier humans, and to improve the lot of those to come.
paragraphs.zh: 这种长远视角，使得对人类前景的悲观看法更像是一时的风潮。诚然，未来并非一片玫瑰色。但我们如今掌握的知识已经足够丰富，能够降低许多曾威胁早期人类生存的风险，并改善后代的命运。
